status: proposal only; no implementation or experiment

sources.title: Appropriate uses for SQLite
sources.observation: SQLite targets local embedded storage; client/server systems serve different requirements.

sources.title: SQLite C/C++ interface introduction
sources.observation: Connections/statements, prepare/bind/step/column and finalization provide a small native binding entry point.

sources.title: PostgreSQL libpq C library
sources.observation: An existing C client is a candidate later native adapter; this review did not build or test it.

sources.title: PostgreSQL command execution
sources.observation: PQexecParams separates parameters from SQL and uses $1-style placeholders.

sources.title: Redis hiredis C guide
sources.observation: Redis provides a documented C client candidate for a separately selected key-value API.

sources.title: SQLite security guidance
sources.observation: Defensive configuration, engine limits and authorization reduce attack exposure; native library bugs remain possible.

sources.title: SQLite compile-time authorization callbacks
sources.observation: The engine can deny operations during statement preparation; access policy must cover schema/attachment/function behavior.

sources.title: SQLite query progress callbacks
sources.observation: A nonzero callback result interrupts work. This alone does not establish full wall-clock or memory bounds.

recommendations_as_inference: Start with a SQLite C adapter and a small SQL library together for the current local standalone app.
Keep key-value/document APIs separate; share applicable policy/error/observability conventions.
Use a second actual SQL driver to validate common API semantics; keep dialect differences explicit.
Define driver ownership, rollback cleanup, grants and native execution limits before implementation.
deferred: exact public names and launch grants
negative_findings: Current Native catalog cannot load arbitrary database libraries or provide the required file/network authority.
SQL dialects and NoSQL semantics cannot be promised interchangeable by a connection wrapper.
Current pure Fn callbacks cannot execute arbitrary database actions in a transaction helper.
Lobo expression fuel does not bound work inside a native database call.
Try can skip explicit cleanup if used without a result-owning transaction boundary.
